<reason>CON controlled the decisive frame: the motion's purpose clause is disease prevention, and PRO conceded "the disease outcome is the same" as donor-egg IVF, so the marginal spend buys relatedness plus reversion risk. CON then turned PRO's strongest point (homoplasmic mothers) into a liability by noting that cohort is where carryover is entirely pathogenic, and caught PRO's staged/registry proposal as describing a trial rather than funded standard care. PRO fought well — the PGD funding precedent and "rationing is about how, not whether" were real hits, and the natural-conception counterfactual was left partly unanswered because CON's second rebuttal clipped — but PRO also lost material to two clipped speeches and never fully neutralized the failure-mode asymmetry (PGD failure = no pregnancy; MRT failure = a sick child with heritable disease). A competitive debate, but CON made it easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B2.1–B2.5: CON seized PRO's own admission that egg donation removes the mother as genetic parent, reframed MRT as a rationed fertility service, and flipped the homoplasmic minority argument by showing the technique is least reliable exactly where PRO says it is uniquely needed. PRO's A4.1 reply ("the disease outcome is the same") cemented rather than escaped the trap.</best_rebuttal>
